## 1. Install and load

Install once. After an update, restart R before loading FunMel. In RStudio,
choose **Session → Restart R**.

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
```

```{r load}
library(FunMel)
```

Source installation requires Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools
on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on
Linux. R >= 4.1 is required. To install the tutorials for offline use, add
`build_vignettes=TRUE` to `install_github()`.

## 2. Prepare the real-data example

Run these steps in order. The eight photographs contain two sets, each with
three fungal confrontation plates and one control plate. The supplied metadata
already identifies each plate's treatment, own control and segmentation layout;
no metadata entry or approval-flag edits are needed for this example.

```{r prepare-real}
photos <- system.file("extdata", "14-days", package="FunMel")
project_dir <- tempfile("FunMel_real_example_")
project <- prepare_experiment(input=photos, project_dir=project_dir)
project$project_dir
```

`tempfile()` supplies a new temporary folder name, so repeating the example
creates a separate project without overwriting earlier work. Keep the printed
folder location: all outputs will be saved there. To retain this practice run,
copy the complete project folder to a permanent location before closing R.

## 3. Measure and inspect

The 90-mm diameter below is an **illustrative calibration**. Verify the actual
outer dish diameter before using measurements scientifically. The workflow
measures the four target colonies on each plate and requests five circular
spots per colony.

```{r measure-real}
result <- run_experiment(
  project, dish_diameter_mm=90, max_dim=1200,
  n_spots=5, spot_radius_mm=0.4, n_boot=20
)
result$analysis_status
result$failed
project$qc_dir
```

The expected status is `"complete"` with zero failed photographs. Open the
printed QC folder and inspect the target-colony masks, central fungal tissue
and hyphae, sampling spots, scale and lighting before interpreting results.
`result$run_summary` separates image completion from colony completeness;
`measurement_issues.csv` names missing colonies or incomplete spot sampling.
QC reminders do not require changing approval flags. Resolve genuine failed
photographs before finalizing. The 20 bootstrap resamples keep this practice
run quick; they are not intended for precise uncertainty estimates.

Inspect the measurements directly:

```{r measurements-real}
knitr::kable(head(result$colonies[c("plate_id", "colony_id", "MI_mean")]),
             digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(head(result$spots[c("plate_id", "colony_id", "spot_id", "MI_mean")]),
             digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

## 4. Calculate coefficients and display the final figure

Finalization reuses the saved measurements and matches each treatment to its
own set's control.

```{r finish-real}
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
knitr::kable(reviewed$melanization_coefficient[
  c("set_id", "treatment", "MI_treatment_mean", "MI_control_mean",
    "melanization_coefficient", "n_treatment_plates", "n_control_plates")],
  digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

```{r comparison-real}
comparison <- plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed)
if (!is.null(comparison)) print(comparison)
```

The left panel shows plate melanization indices; the right panel shows
matched-control coefficients. Squares are controls, circles are treatment
plates and lower diamonds are treatment means. Bars show one between-plate
SD, not confidence intervals. Each set has only one control, so control SD
and replicated-control significance tests are unavailable.

MI is `100 - CIELAB L*`, an image-darkness proxy rather than a direct measurement
of melanin concentration. Colonies and spots within a plate are subsamples;
independent plates are the experimental units. See the
[detailed real-data tutorial](Real-14-day.html) for interpretation and limitations.

## 5. Find outputs and reopen saved work

```{r outputs-real}
project$project_dir
```

This folder contains colony, spot, profile and plate CSV tables; matched
coefficients; saved R analyses; QC images; and the final
`treatment_comparison.pdf`, `.svg` and `.png`. Statistics and the explanatory
caption are saved separately. The exported figure has no embedded caption
by default.

After saving or moving the **complete** project folder, reopen it without
preparing or measuring again:

```{r reopen-real, eval=FALSE}
project <- load_experiment() # Select project.rds in the saved project folder.
result <- read_experiment(project)
reviewed <- read_experiment(project, finalized=TRUE)
print(plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed))
```

## Use your own photographs

Follow the [own-ZIP workflow](Real-14-day.html#standalone-alternative-analyze-your-own-14-day-zip)
for separate input/output paths, preparation, reopening and measurement.
Your photographs may have any supported names and any actual treatment codes;
the bundled assignments apply only to the supplied photographs.

Measurements do not require treatment names or approval flags. A mixed collection
still needs correct per-image layouts: `fungus` for confrontations and `none`
for controls. Matched coefficients need real treatment/control assignments
within `set_id`; otherwise measurements are saved with `awaiting_design`.
For exploration without treatment names, use the
[set-only measurement plot](Real-14-day.html#explore-measurements-by-set-without-treatment-names).
Missing target MI instead produces `awaiting_measurement_review` and identifies
the affected plate/colony. Use the [real-data troubleshooting guide](Real-14-day.html#when-coefficient-tables-are-empty)
for diagnostics, control assignment and the correct reanalysis procedure.
Every custom metadata column is retained.

For specialist calibration, classification and measurement utilities, see the
[complete function examples](Function-examples.html).
